title: Splitting text lines and inline shader reveal
blurb: Live editable essay inside an ElementGL WebGL 2 canvas. Hovering, tapping or selecting an anchor word slides neighbouring text lines apart vertically while animated GPU pixel blocks or an iridescent optical ribbon fill the opened slot.
question: Can hovering, tapping or selecting an anchor keyword inside a live editable HTML essay cause surrounding lines to slide apart vertically, holding the word steady inside an illuminated slot while GPU pixel blocks or an optical GLSL ribbon fill the gap, with zero DOM text reflow and working links and selection?
result: Not verified in a live browser yet. One ElementGL context slices a single texElementSubImage2D() essay texture across three horizontal strips from cached Range.getClientRects() line bounds, keeps the anchored <button> hit-testable via updateElementGeometry() scaled by geometryUnit(), and falls back to 9-argument drawElementImage() slices or plain HTML.
